subject: Init token pacing & streaming approach for Streamly pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ellis <sam@streamly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Init token pacing & streaming approach for Streamly pilot

Hi Sam — great conversation earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single reference point.

Key performance targets discussed:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): Streamly target = <= 150 ms average, 95th <= 350 ms for interactive chat flows. You flagged that mobile users should feel <200 ms most of the time.
- Throughput / concurrency: Pilot baseline = 50 concurrent live streams / ~300 QPS peak for burst patterns.
- Streaming behavior: preferred chunk cadence 200–400 ms per chunk for low-latency UX; chunk granularity = sentence or ~128–256 token windows (whichever finishes first).

SSE vs WebSocket:
- We recommended WebSocket for the pilot for its bi-directional control and lower header overhead on long-lived sessions; SSE still supported for browser fallbacks and simpler server setups.
- For Streamly we suggested starting with WebSocket (primary) + SSE fallback; Redwood runtime can run both and route by client capability.

Technical notes & constraints we captured:
- Model: you want to test a 13B open model (sampling-based, temperature 0.7) and one quantized variant for cost comparisons.
- KV/prefix caching: expected to reduce per-request token work for repeat prompts — will enable on pilot.
- Tokenization: average response token churn ~200 tokens in the first 3s of streaming on your sample set.

Attachments: sending the perf requirements doc and a redlined MA template for procurement review (attached).

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
1) Redwood test harness + perf script: Ben to provision harness and sample workload by end of week (action: ben@redwood.com).
2) Pilot environment & credentials: Aisha to share pilot scope and sign-off checklist for legal/procurement (action: aisha@redwood.com).
3) Pilot start date: target week of Aug 10 — two-week ramp + 1 week of acceptance testing.

Questions for you before we lock schedules:
- Are you comfortable with WebSocket as primary, SSE as fallback?
- Confirm the 50 concurrent streams / 300 QPS baseline or share a different traffic profile.

Thanks again — I’ll kick off Ben on the harness once you confirm the above.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[aisha@redwood.com]

- streamly_perf_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf)
- redwood_ma_template_redlined.docx (docx)
From: Sam Ellis <sam@streamly.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Init token pacing & streaming approach for Streamly pilot

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the detailed recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) TTFT goals: our product team is comfortable with a 150 ms average TTFT but we need 95th <= 400 ms (not 350) for the first release due to variable mobile network conditions. Can we capture both the 50/95/99 percentiles in the pilot metrics?

2) Streaming transport: we prefer WebSocket as primary (we have an existing connection manager that ties to our presence service). SSE fallback is good for lighter clients.

3) Concurrency/throughput: the 50 concurrent streams is a good baseline. Our internal stress test shows occasional peaks to 420 QPS for short bursts — can the pilot include a 10-minute burst test at 400–450 QPS?

4) Chunk cadence: 200–400 ms cadence sounds right. For us, minimizing chunk framing (avoid very small chunks) is important to keep CPU + memory overhead predictable. Sentences or ~150 token windows is fine.

Pilot timeline: Aug 10 works for a soft start. We prefer the following acceptance criteria:
- TTFT median <= 150 ms, 95th <= 400 ms on your staging infra under our sample workload.
- <1% error rate for streaming connections under 50 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput: sustain 300 QPS baseline and survive 10-minute 450 QPS burst with <5% degradation to TTFT.

I will share a short CSV of sample prompts and a few representative client traces (network + device). Also looping in our engineering lead Priya (copying offline) for integration questions.

If you can confirm Ben will own the test harness and provide the measurement dashboards, we’ll lock the pilot dates.

—Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Integrations | Streamly Inc.
sam@streamly.io
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Init token pacing & streaming approach for Streamly pilot

Looping in our internal runbook and next actions based on Sam’s clarifications.

Acceptance metrics (what we'll measure):
- TTFT (median, p50/p95/p99) measured at the app edge with synthetic clients that mimic mobile RTT distribution.
- Per-chunk latency and inter-chunk cadence distribution (ms).
- Streaming connection error rate and reconnect frequency.
- Throughput: sustained RPS and burst window behavior (10-minute window at 450 QPS).
- CPU/GPU utilization and token-cost breakdown per request (to inform quantized model vs full precision).

Test harness plan (owner: Ben):
- Build script to replay Sam's CSV of prompts across simulated clients (mobile RTT emulation, WebSocket + SSE modes).
- Run baseline (50 concurrent) + burst profile (450 QPS) in Redwood staging; collect metrics to a Grafana dashboard.
- Export raw traces and a summary CSV for Streamly.

Timing & deliverables:
- Friday (Jul 31): initial harness + sample run on 50 concurrent, preliminary metric snapshots.
- Wed Aug 5: full burst test + dashboard link ready for review.
- Aug 10: soft pilot start with customer traffic.

Immediate asks for Aisha (to unblock):
- Share Sam’s CSV and any mobile client-network profiles (RTT/packet loss) — Sam mentioned he’d send these.
- Confirm any legal/procurement gating items from the redlined MA doc (Aisha).

I’ll attach the harness README and a perf checklist; will also create the HubSpot deal link and attach runbook notes.

Ben Carter
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
